title: emwc-world-heavyweight
label: Gabriel Whitecross

won.source: Already champion entering An Evening To The Extreme (26 January 1998); no document in the held record dates the reign's start.

note: Billed to defend the title against The Inkinator, winner of that night's twenty-man battle royal, on An Evening To The Extreme (26 January 1998); the surviving record does not carry that match's own finish. The title had changed hands by 7 April 1999, when "Crimson" Joe Reed is billed as champion; no document in the held record dates or details the transfer.

title: emwc-world-television
label: "Precious" Pietro Sandini

won.source: Already champion entering An Evening To The Extreme (26 January 1998); no document in the held record dates the reign's start.

note: Successfully defended the title against Dirt Dog Unique Allah in a Double Title Ladder Match on An Evening To The Extreme (26 January 1998). The title had changed hands by 7 April 1999, when Eddie Van Gibson is billed as champion; no document in the held record dates or details the transfer.

title: emwc-north-american
label: Sam Willis

won.source: An Evening To The Extreme, 7 April 1999: defeated Zack Malone by pinfall after the assigned referee, Juan Diablo, was knocked unconscious and a fill-in referee made the count.

note: Won the title from Zack Malone in a contested finish; the broadcast frames the deciding count as controversial.

title: emwc-world-heavyweight
label: "Crimson" Joe Reed

won.source: Billed as EMWC World Heavyweight Champion entering An Evening To The Extreme, 7 April 1999; no document in the held record dates the transfer from the prior champion.

note: Retained the title against Youth Gone Wild with the Kentucky Backsmasher on 7 April 1999.

title: emwc-world-television
label: Eddie Van Gibson

won.source: Billed as EMWC World Television Champion entering An Evening To The Extreme, 7 April 1999; no document in the held record dates the transfer from the prior champion.

note: Retained the title against V.D. Vitrone, a lottery-drawn mystery challenger making his EMWC debut, with the Canuckle Duster on 7 April 1999.

title: emwc-north-american
label: Dirt Dog Unique Allah

won.source: Already champion entering An Evening To The Extreme (26 January 1998); no document in the held record dates the reign's start.

note: Successfully defended the title against Pietro Sandini in a Double Title Ladder Match on An Evening To The Extreme (26 January 1998), despite his own tag partner Tony Starks turning on him mid-match. The title had changed hands by 7 April 1999, when "The Attack" Zack Malone is billed as champion; no document in the held record dates or details the transfer.

title: emwc-north-american
label: "The Attack" Zack Malone

won.source: Billed as EMWC North American Champion entering An Evening To The Extreme, 7 April 1999; no document in the held record dates the transfer from the prior champion.

note: Lost the title to Sam Willis on 7 April 1999 after the assigned referee was knocked unconscious and a fill-in referee made the count.

title: emwc-world-tag-team
label: The Epitome of Cool

won.source: An Evening To The Extreme, 7 April 1999: defeated Zokugun Sangai (TORA and Akuma) by pinfall (a reverse DDT by Dan Thomas) after a back-and-forth title match.

note: Won the EMWC World Tag Team Championship.

title: emwc-world-tag-team
label: Zokugun Sangai

won.source: Billed as EMWC World Tag Team Champions entering An Evening To The Extreme, 7 April 1999; no document in the held record dates when or from whom they won the title.

note: Lost the title to The Epitome of Cool on 7 April 1999.

title: emwc-junior-heavyweight
label: Youth Gone Wild

won.source: An Evening To The Extreme, 7 April 1999: pinned champion "Righteous" Richard Blue with a top-of-the-cage Wildflyer after Blue was left unable to defend himself by an outside attack.

note: Won the title the same night he also challenged unsuccessfully for the EMWC World Heavyweight Championship.

title: emwc-junior-heavyweight
label: "Righteous" Richard Blue

won.source: Billed as EMWC Junior Heavyweight Champion entering An Evening To The Extreme, 7 April 1999; the broadcast's own commentary attributes the win to help from Steve "The Fury" Kowalski, with no document in the held record dating or detailing the match itself.

note: Attacked in the cage before the bell by Steve "The Fury" Kowalski while defending the title against Youth Gone Wild on 7 April 1999, then lost by pinfall while unable to defend himself, on the order of the promotion's own returning former president.
